project_tracker_diagnostic: Low multi-trunked shrub/small tree on dry limestone; flaky/papery bark; variable shallowly lobed leaves; very shallow saucer-like acorn cup enclosing about one-quarter of the nut or less.
verified_target_counties: Hays; Travis; Blanco; Burnet; Comal; Gillespie; Kerr; Bandera; Edwards; Real; Uvalde; Crockett; Kimble

morphology_keys.habit: Shrub or small tree usually to about 3–5 m, often forming thickets with multiple trunks near ground level.
morphology_keys.bark: Gray to light brown, flaky to papery and exfoliating.
morphology_keys.leaves: Highly variable, from nearly entire to irregularly toothed or sinuately lobed; underside often has minute appressed stellate hairs.
morphology_keys.acorn: Cup saucer-shaped to shallowly cup-shaped, generally enclosing only about 1/8–1/4 of the nut.
best_field_traits: FNA variety: commonly 0.5–3(–5) m and multi-stemmed; adult leaf blade typically 30–60 × 20–40 mm.
Q. sinuata leaf undersides vary from silvery minute appressed stellate hairs to nearly hairless, especially in shade leaves. Do not use apparent hairlessness as a species exclusion.
FNA species-level twigs about 1–2(–3) mm, mostly glabrous; buds ovoid, 2–3 mm.
Acorn nut 7–12(–15) mm long; shallow saucer cup about 3–8 mm deep × 8–12 mm broad (varietal description), commonly enclosing around 1/4 nut or less; scales flat and closely appressed.
Plants along streams can approach intermediates with Q. sinuata var. sinuata; require habit, environment, and multiple organs before assigning variety.

photo_strategy.oak_specific_tightening: Prioritize multi-photo late-summer/fall observations to increase the chance of mature leaves and acorns, plus curated taxon reference photos.

look_here_first: Use the whole plant first: a dry-limestone shrub or small multi-stemmed tree, commonly a low thicket. Then inspect bud, mature leaf underside, and ripe acorn cup—the cup scales are flattened, NOT strongly tuberculate. Leaf outline alone is unreliable.

diagnostic_comparison.method: Read habit, mature leaf and underside, bud, and ripe cupule together; avoid a single-leaf ID.

pair_specific_tie_breakers.quercus-laceyi: Lacey oak has bluer glaucous leaves, buds and a taller single/less thicket-like habit on average; its acorn is more often barrel-shaped with a moderately tuberculate cup. White shin has flatter cup scales and smaller fruit.
pair_specific_tie_breakers.quercus-vaseyana: White shin is usually deciduous, broad- or variably lobed, with 7–11 secondary veins per side; Vasey is evergreen/subevergreen with narrow leaves and 4–6 secondary veins, dark shredding bark and strongly tuberculate cup scales.

diagnostic_comparison.field_uncertainty: Retain Quercus sp. or the pair-level comparison if intermediates / absent fruit prevent a reliable determination.

needs: Habit: low multistem limestone thicket with trunk bases visible
Leaf underside under 10–20× magnification to show appressed stellate hairs (sun AND shade material)
Acorn cup rim and lateral scales photographed macro to document NONtuberculate flattened scales
Entire mature leaf with ruler and 7–11 lateral veins annotated only after photo inspection
Terminal bud with mm scale and bark close-up
